To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Internet plays a key role in helping prostate cancer patients make treatment decisions; (2) physicians are the key source of medical information for patients; (3) there is a need for more information related to treatment and treatment side effects; and (4) physicians want to receive information directly from agencies and meet with them one-on-on.

1) patients and their families use the Internet as a primary channel to make informed prostate cancer decisions, 2) the Internet is an important channel for physicians to provide information about prostate cancer, and 3) physicians are the most important information source for patients.

prostate cancer treatment decision making is an important area of research that can be improved through the development of online information resources that can be disseminated to patients, physicians, and other relevant stakeholders.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effectiveness of online prostate cancer treatment information and its dissemination to those who need this information the most.
how online prostate cancer decision-making information can best be disseminated, and how it can be improved to meet the information needs of those affected by this disease.
the development of a theoretical framework to understand how online prostate cancer information is currently disseminated and how it can be improved.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study provides a framework to guide organizations in their efforts to improve the quality and dissemination of online prostate cancer treatment information.

the best way to improve prostate cancer information dissemination is to provide physicians with the most current and accurate treatment options, and treatment side effect information that can be easily accessed and delivered to patients.

there is a need for prostate cancer organizations to improve the information that they offer to patients and to disseminate this information to patients and their physicians in ways that are more accessible, timely, and relevant to the decision-making process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the best way to improve dissemination of online prostate cancer information is for organizations to provide the most up-to-date and accurate information possible, make it accessible and easy to understand, and to reach out to physicians to ensure they have access to this information.
the Internet is an excellent channel through which to reach prostate cancer patients with treatment-related information.

the Internet can serve as a powerful tool for prostate cancer patients, their family members, physicians, and prostate cancer organizations, if it is used in a way that is consistent with how patients make decisions and how they prefer to receive information.
The main takeaway from our work is that
organizations should continue to improve their prostate cancer treatment information offerings and disseminate them through the Internet.
the Internet is a valuable source of information for prostate cancer patients and family members, but the information provided must be more easily accessible and relevant to their needs.

organizations can improve the effectiveness of their online prostate cancer treatment information dissemination efforts by: 1) providing more accessible, easy-to-understand treatment options information, 2) providing more accessible and easy-to-understand information about treatment side effects, and 3) reaching out directly to physicians to provide them with information to share with their patients.
